decisions.statement: A swap writes the ask into the seat's uncommitted values.
The ask a swap writes is spelled as the page with that name is spelled.
The gateway alone is respawned.
The gateway is respawned on the port the gateway already had.
A seat with no live gateway is passed over rather than refused.
A swap reaches one seat or every live seat.
A swap naming no seat and no fleet is refused.
A swap naming a seat and the fleet together is refused rather than chosen between.
A second seat named beside the first is refused.
Every seat a fleet swap reaches is acted on rather than a stop at the first seat not answering.
A fleet swap is staggered.
Nothing here restarts a client.
Nothing here arms a further act on the seat this command swapped.
A seat that did not take the swap up before the wait ran out is refused as an operational fault.
Each seat is named as soon as that seat holds the ask.
A swap that threw part way names those seats in its refusal.
A swap that refused part way names them as a swap that threw does.
Naming them leaves what a swap reports as it was, so json stays json.
A seat holding the ask swaps whether or not this call lives to say so.
The asking, the seat lookup and the roster this reaches are handed in.
A seat may also be named by its id rather than as its page is named.

definition: the command respawning a live seat's gateway on the bytecode here
